relationships.description: R. M. Barrington-Ward was assistant editor in 1927–1941 and succeeded Dawson as editor in 1941.

relationships.label: Regius Professor of Modern History
relationships.description: Davis returned from Manchester to Oxford in 1925 as Regius Professor of Modern History, succeeding Charles Firth.

relationships.label: Wartime research based at Oxford
relationships.description: The Institute’s research collections and personnel were transferred to Oxford and established in Balliol, All Souls and Rhodes House as FRPS.

relationships.label: Covenant legal drafting attributed by Quigley
relationships.description: Quigley attributes the wording of crucial League Covenant articles to Hurst, comparing their legal loopholes with those he says Hurst drafted into the Locarno Pacts. This is the author’s appraisal of treaty drafting, not an assertion of League employment.

profileUpdates.description: Quigley identifies Birchenough as Milner’s former roommate, a British South Africa Company director from 1905 and president from 1925, and a Beit Fund trustee from 1920. These reported appointments are distinct from his tentative Society of the Elect placement in the appendix.

Master of Balliol from 1916 until 1924; Quigley describes his close friendship with Brassey and collaboration with the Round Table after 1910. The Society of the Elect roster remains Quigley’s tentative political classification.

Named by Quigley as Beit Lecturer in Colonial History at Oxford in 1930–1935. His inner-circle placement in the appendix is tentative; an academic appointment does not independently prove that political classification.

Quigley identifies Davis as an All Souls and Balliol fellow, medieval historian, organizer of the Foreign Office War Trade Intelligence Department, and later Regius Professor of Modern History at Oxford. His tentative outer-circle roster classification is separate from these reported roles.

All Souls fellow from 1910 and Warden in 1933–1945, Gladstone Professor in 1912–1933, and secretary to Lloyd George in 1916–1919. Quigley distinguishes these appointments from his Milner Group classification.

All Souls fellow in 1907–1914, Balliol fellow and tutor in 1919–1941, and Beit Lecturer in Colonial History in 1924–1927. His political-network placement derives from Quigley’s tentative appendix and interpretive account.

Quigley describes Somervell as an All Souls fellow who entered Parliament in 1931 and served as Solicitor General, Attorney General, Home Secretary and then Lord Justice of Appeal. His outer-circle appendix placement remains the author’s classification.

Quigley identifies Peacock as a Rhodes Trustee, Bank of England director in 1921–1946, and wartime British Treasury representative in Washington. He expressly leaves uncertain whether Peacock represented Milner Group interests, despite close Canadian personal connections and the appendix listing.

Quigley describes Woodward’s All Souls fellowship, Balliol fellowship, New College teaching, Chatham House council service and appointment as Montague Burton Professor in 1944. His outer-circle network placement is interpretive rather than implied by any one academic role.

Quigley describes R. M. Barrington-Ward as assistant editor of The Times in 1927–1941 and Dawson’s successor as editor in 1941. His brother married A. L. Smith’s daughter; this must not be converted into a marriage involving the editor himself. His appendix classification remains tentative.

Quigley identifies Steel-Maitland as an All Souls fellow, Colonial Office Parliamentary Under Secretary in 1915–1917, overseas-trade official jointly in the Foreign Office and Board of Trade in 1917–1919, and Minister of Labour in 1924–1929. These are actual reported offices, distinct from the appendix classification.
Quigley records Harris’s election to the RIIA council in 1924 and his participation in the Institute’s early discussion meetings. His outer-circle appendix placement remains tentative.
Quigley names MacDonald among RIIA council members and dates his election to 1933. The separate outer-circle roster classification does not establish formal membership in a secret organization.

Oxford’s Beit Professor of Colonial History in 1905–1920 and an All Souls fellow until 1927. Quigley expressly places him in the Cecil Bloc, Round Table and Milner Group, while his academic appointment and fellowship provide distinct institutional links.

Quigley identifies Goschen and Peacock as Bank of England directors and records the Bank’s 1926 gift to RIIA and inclusion in 1929 annual-grant pledges. These specific ties do not establish that the Milner Group owned or controlled the Bank.
Named among the corporations pledging annual grants to RIIA in 1929. The cited list supports a donor relationship, without specifying the amount or asserting political control of the company.
Named among the banks pledging annual grants to RIIA in 1929. The cited list supports a funding relationship, without specifying the amount or political control of the bank.

Quigley describes the League-associated International Labour Office through Harold Butler’s deputy directorship in 1920–1932 and directorship in 1932–1938. The institutional appointment supports an explicit affiliation rather than only an event co-occurrence.

Quigley identifies Greene as secretary to the Peace Conference Reparations Commission in 1919 and Salter as his successor in 1920–1922. The record refers to the Allied reparations administration and its staff roles.

Existing identifiable pledgers were linked; the remaining names need distinct source-cited organization records.

summary: Audited all 240 Anglo-American Establishment profiles against cited passages, existing source-qualified relationships and related event records. Checked the tentative appendix separately from concrete appointments, corporate directorships, fellowships, donations, committee roles and institutional mergers. Additions use explicit body statements; co-occurrence and shared institutional membership are not treated as personal relationships. Existing generic association edges are retained without redundant specific-role edges for the same pair. Unresolved entries document bounded identity and qualification gaps.
